action.gmail.label: label an email “{label}” ({id})
action.gmail.trash: move an email to the trash ({id})
approval.suggest: You’ve allowed this 3 times. Always allow it, without asking?
catalog.externalHelp: External connector in {dir}. It runs as a separate process and only gets the variables below.
catalog.remoteHelp: Remote MCP server at {url}. It only gets what Zodim sends it, with the headers below.
msg.approval.always: Allowed. This won’t be asked again.
msg.approval.batch: Allowed for the rest of this run.
msg.approval.gone: This request is no longer waiting.
msg.email.where: The result arrives on Telegram, WhatsApp or in Needs you.
msg.explore.noRoutine: This can’t become a routine because the data it needs couldn’t be read ({what}). Fix that and ask again.
msg.explore.offer: Turn this into a routine, without paying for a model every time?
msg.explore.simulated_one: ({count} action was only simulated; nothing was changed.)
msg.explore.simulated_other: ({count} actions were only simulated; nothing was changed.)
msg.ownerOnly: Only the owner of the house can do that.
msg.pair.already: Zodim is already connected here. Ask for something you do every week.
msg.pair.badCode: That code doesn’t match. Open Connections in Zodim and use the code shown there.
msg.pair.link: Hi! Zodim is connected here too. Ask for something you do every week.
msg.pair.linkBad: That code doesn’t match. See the pairing code in Connections.
msg.pair.owner:
Hi, {name}! Zodim is connected. 👋

Ask for something you do every week, for example:
• “Every day at 7am, send me my calendar and the important emails”

The first time, Zodim does it while you watch. After that, on its own.
msg.pair.person: Hi, {name}! You can now talk to the house’s Zodim. Ask for something you do every week.
msg.pair.whatsapp: Hi! Zodim is connected on WhatsApp too. Ask for something you do every week.
msg.pair.whatsappBad: That code doesn’t match. Get a new one in Connections or People.
msg.pair.whatsappPerson: Hi, {name}! You can now talk to the house’s Zodim on WhatsApp.
msg.photo.ask: See what to do with this
msg.request.started: Got it. Working on it now; the result will arrive here. 🔎
msg.routine.redo: Redoing it with the agent; the result will arrive here.
msg.routine.reran: Ran again and it worked. Routine turned back on.
msg.upgrade: Zodim was updated from {from} to {to}. A copy of everything as it was before is kept: if something looks wrong, go to Settings › Backup › Local copies and go back to it.
rule.preset-changes: Ask me before any change, even reversible ones.
rule.preset-delete: Deleting always becomes moving to the trash.
rule.preset-irreversible: Always ask me before anything that can’t be undone.
rule.preset-others: Only ask me before sending something to other people.
svc.discord.description: Alerts in a Discord channel of yours.
svc.discord.field.webhook.label: Webhook
svc.discord.help: In the channel, Edit channel › Integrations › Webhooks › New webhook, and copy the address.
svc.discord.title: Discord — alerts in a channel
svc.discordchat.description: Talk to Zodim by private message on Discord.
svc.discordchat.field.token.label: Bot token
svc.discordchat.help: At discord.com/developers/applications, create an app, go to Bot, generate the token and invite the bot to a server of yours. Then send it, in a private message: zodim and the pairing code from Connections.
svc.discordchat.title: Discord
svc.github.description: Issues and pull requests of your repositories.
svc.github.field.token.label: Token
svc.github.help: Create a fine-grained token at github.com/settings/tokens with read-only access to issues, and write access if Zodim should comment.
svc.github.title: GitHub
svc.homeassistant.field.token.label: Long-lived token
svc.homeassistant.field.url.label: Home Assistant address
svc.homeassistant.help: In Home Assistant › Profile › Security, create a long-lived token. Locks, alarms, gates and valves always ask for your approval.
svc.homeassistant.title: Home Assistant
svc.notion.field.token.label: Integration token
svc.notion.help: Create an internal integration at notion.so/my-integrations and share with it only the pages Zodim may see.
svc.notion.title: Notion
svc.obsidian.description: Your Markdown notes, in the vault folder.
svc.obsidian.field.vault.label: Vault folder
svc.obsidian.help: Give the vault folder on this computer. Before changing a note, Zodim keeps a copy in .zodim/history.
svc.obsidian.title: Obsidian
svc.rss.description: Reads news feeds, blogs and releases.
svc.rss.help: Nothing to set up: each routine declares the sites it may read.
svc.rss.title: RSS and Atom
svc.signal.description: Talk to Zodim on Signal, encrypted up to this computer.
svc.signal.field.account.label: Zodim’s number on Signal
svc.signal.field.url.label: signal-cli address
svc.signal.help: Install signal-cli, register or link a number and keep it running: signal-cli -a +NUMBER daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8080. Then send to that number, from your Signal: zodim and the pairing code from Connections.
svc.signal.title: Signal
svc.slack.description: Alerts in a Slack channel of yours.
svc.slack.field.webhook.label: Webhook
svc.slack.help: Create an app at api.slack.com/apps with Incoming Webhooks for a channel of your own and paste the webhook address.
svc.slack.title: Slack — alerts in a channel
svc.slackchat.description: Talk to Zodim by direct message on Slack.
svc.slackchat.field.app_token.label: App token (xapp-)
svc.slackchat.field.bot_token.label: Bot token (xoxb-)
svc.slackchat.help: At api.slack.com/apps, create an app, turn on Socket Mode (it creates the xapp- token with connections:write), subscribe to the message.im event, give the bot im:history, im:write and chat:write, and install it in the workspace. Then send the app, in a direct message: zodim and the pairing code from Connections.
svc.slackchat.title: Slack
svc.todoist.description: Your tasks: read, create and complete.
svc.todoist.field.token.label: API token
svc.todoist.help: In Todoist › Settings › Integrations › Developer, copy the API token.
svc.todoist.title: Todoist
svc.websearch.description: Searches the internet: news, prices, opening hours, anything.
svc.websearch.field.brave_key.label: Brave Search API key
svc.websearch.field.searxng_url.label: SearXNG address
svc.websearch.help: Use the Brave Search API (free key at api-dashboard.search.brave.com, 2,000 searches a month) or the address of a SearXNG instance of your own or one you trust, with the JSON format turned on. If both are filled in, Brave is used.
svc.websearch.title: Web search
